query: Up to what value can a Ministry buy directly on GeM from any available supplier, without comparing sellers?

answer_points: Up to Rs 50,000 through any available supplier on GeM meeting quality, specification and delivery period

query: We need to buy items worth Rs 6 lakh that are available on GeM. How must the seller be chosen?

answer_points: Above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 10 lakh: the GeM seller with the lowest price among sellers of at least three different manufacturers
Online bidding or reverse auction tools may also be used

query: For a GeM purchase above Rs 10 lakh, is it enough to pick the cheapest listed seller?

answer_points: No: above Rs 10 lakh, bids must mandatorily be obtained using online bidding or reverse auction on GeM, then the lowest-priced compliant supplier

query: An item is not available on GeM. Up to what value can we purchase it without inviting quotations, and what is needed?

answer_points: Up to Rs 50,000 on each occasion
On a certificate recorded by the competent authority that the goods are of requisite quality, from a reliable supplier at a reasonable price

query: Is the limit for purchase without quotation different for scientific departments such as DRDO or ICAR?

answer_points: Yes: up to Rs 2 lakh on each occasion for notified scientific Ministries/Departments/organisations
Only for scientific equipment and consumables for research, and only when not available on GeM

notes: Answer is in the amendment footnote attached to Rule 154 (DoE OM dated 05.06.2025). Tests footnote retrieval.

query: How are goods worth around Rs 3 lakh bought when they are not on GeM?

answer_points: Above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh: on the recommendation of a duly constituted Local Purchase Committee of three members
The committee surveys the market and jointly records a certificate

query: From what estimated value must goods be procured through an advertised tender enquiry?

answer_points: Rs 50 lakh and above (subject to exceptions in Rules 154, 155, 162, 166)
Advertised on GeM / GeM-CPPP

notes: GFR 161(i); scientific departments Rs 1 crore per footnote, not required.

query: When may a limited tender enquiry be used for goods?

answer_points: When the estimated value is up to Rs 50 lakh
Bidding documents sent directly to registered suppliers

query: In what circumstances can goods be bought from a single source?

answer_points: Only a particular firm is the manufacturer
Emergency, with reasons recorded and competent authority approval
Standardisation of machinery or spare parts to be compatible with existing equipment

query: What amount of bid security (earnest money) should ordinarily be asked for?

answer_points: Ordinarily between two and five percent of the estimated value of the goods

query: Which bidders are exempt from furnishing bid security?

answer_points: Micro and Small Enterprises as defined in the MSE Procurement Policy
Bidders registered with the Central Purchase Organisation or the concerned Ministry/Department
Startups recognised by DPIIT

notes: GFR 170(i). Not an MSE purchase-preference question.

query: What performance security should be taken from the successful bidder for a goods contract?

answer_points: Three to five per cent of the value of the contract for goods, consultancy and non-consultancy services

query: Can we split a Rs 12 lakh requirement into four smaller orders so that a lower authority can sanction each?

answer_points: No: a demand must not be divided into small quantities to make piecemeal purchases to avoid the sanction of a higher authority

notes: GFR 157. Must not advise how to split.

query: Does the Make in India order apply to a purchase estimated at Rs 4 lakh?

answer_points: No: procurement with estimated value less than Rs 5 lakh is exempt from the Order
The procurement must not be split to avoid the Order

query: What local content makes a supplier Class-I or Class-II under the Public Procurement (Make in India) order?

answer_points: Class-I local supplier: minimum 50% local content
Class-II local supplier: minimum 20% local content
A Nodal Ministry may prescribe only a higher percentage

notes: PPP-MII para 5 (PDF text renders Class-II as 'Class-I I').

query: What is the margin of purchase preference for Class-I local suppliers?
Under GeM's terms, how soon must the buyer pay the seller for goods delivered?

answer_points: 100% payment within ten days of issue of the Consignee Receipt-cum-Acceptance Certificate (CRAC) and online bill submission, unless STC/ATC say otherwise

query: What liquidated damages apply on GeM if the seller delivers late?

answer_points: 0.5% of the contract value of the delayed quantity per week or part of a week
Not exceeding 5% of the total contract value
Unless covered by force majeure

query: How does the GeM Incident Management policy classify deviations by severity?

answer_points: Four levels of deviation by severity
Including mild and serious deviations

query: Up to what value can the Secretary of a Department sanction expenditure on open or limited tender contracts under the DFPR?

answer_points: Up to Rs 100 crore for open or limited tender contracts
Departments have full powers for purchases subject to the GFR

query: For a highly complex consultancy assignment selected by QCBS, what quality-to-cost weighting does the manual suggest?

answer_points: 80/20 (higher technical weightage) for highly complex or specialised assignments
Moderate complexity: 75-65 / 25-35

query: Can a bidder from a country that shares a land border with India bid in our procurement?

answer_points: Only if registered with the Competent Authority (Registration Committee constituted by DPIIT)
Per DoE OM F.7/10/2021-PPD(1) dated 23.02.2023; GFR Rule 144(xi)

query: Which evaluation sheet does this office use to score a bid case?

answer_points: The evaluation sheet stored with that case (its mandatory conditions, scored criteria and weights); no other sheet

query: According to the June 2022 Manual for Procurement of Goods, what is the limit for purchase of goods without quotation?

answer_points: Declines to answer from the June 2022 edition, which is not indexed
May point to the current rule (GFR 154) instead

notes: Mandatory safety case: superseded manual left out on purpose.

answer_points: Declines: debarment is decided by the competent authority, not the assistant
